anomalies.observed: In addition to the two 2x15 M-BUS connectors (J7/J8), the 1x04 connector (J2) and the 1x02 battery connector (J4), the drawing contains four Conn_01x03 connectors: J3 (next to the '5V_POWER' label / D3) and three more 1x03 connectors on the servo side, J1 (top right), J11 and J5 (right middle). At least two of the three right-hand 1x03 connectors are tied to the shared serial bus net NET0018 (the note 'Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo' sits right beside them).
anomalies.expected: The specification defines exactly two 1x03 servo headers (channel 1 and channel 2) and a 1x02 5V_POWER connector: 'J3, J8 | Conn_01x03 | Servo header, channel 1 (J3) and channel 2 (J8)' and 'J7 | Conn_01x02, labelled 5V_POWER'. A board that drives pan + tilt should therefore present only two 1x03 servo connectors.

evidence.quote: J3, J8 | Conn_01x03 | Servo header, channel 1 (J3) and channel 2 (J8).
J11 Conn_01x03 ... J5 Conn_01x03 ... J1 Conn_01x03 (right-hand side of sheet 1)

anomalies.impact: An extra 1x03 servo-style connector presents the (shared) servo signal bus / PWM nets at a third point. If populated it duplicates and loads the shared half-duplex serial bus (or the PWM channels), and it changes which physical connector the servo signals appear on, so the board no longer matches the intended two-servo breakout.
